Getting Started with penguinExplorer

getting-started.Rmd

Introduction

The penguinExplorer package provides an interactive Shiny app for exploring penguin body measurements.

The app is designed for biology students and beginners who want to investigate the following question:

How do penguin body measurements differ across species and islands?

Data

The package contains a cleaned version of the Palmer Penguins dataset.

The original data contains 344 observations. After removing observations with missing body mass, flipper length or bill length, the cleaned dataset contains 342 observations and six variables.

The three penguin species are Adelie, Chinstrap and Gentoo. The observations come from Biscoe, Dream and Torgersen islands.

Source: https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/

Installation

Install the package from GitHub:

install.packages("remotes")

remotes::install_github(
  "ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-ksue0611"
)

Launch the Shiny App

Load the package and launch the app:

library(penguinExplorer)

run_app()

The app opens an interactive interface for exploring the data.

How to Use

  1. Select one or more penguin species using the Species filter.
  2. Select the islands you want to investigate.
  3. Choose body measurements for the X-axis and Y-axis.
  4. Explore the patterns displayed in the scatter plot.
  5. Compare the number of observations and average measurements in the summary table.
  6. Read the Key Finding, which updates based on the selected data.

Understanding the Outputs

Each point in the scatter plot represents one penguin. The colours distinguish Adelie, Chinstrap and Gentoo penguins.

The X-axis and Y-axis represent the measurements selected by the user.

The summary table displays the number of observations, mean body mass in grams and mean flipper length in millimetres for each selected species.

For example, when all species and islands are selected, Gentoo penguins have the highest average body mass, approximately 5076 g.

The Key Finding updates when the selected species or islands change.

Example: Using the Summary Function

The package also includes the exported summarise_penguins() function.

library(penguinExplorer)

summarise_penguins(
  penguins_clean,
  c("Adelie", "Gentoo")
)

This function returns the number of observations, mean body mass and mean flipper length for the selected species.

Limitations

The dataset only includes penguins observed near Palmer Station, Antarctica, and is not representative of all penguin populations.

Species are not equally represented across islands, so differences between islands may also reflect differences in species composition.

The app provides descriptive comparisons and does not establish causal relationships.
